children: Sentiment among consumers in the eurozone inched lower this month, damaged by rebounding energy prices after military action in the Middle East escalated.

The European Commission's flash consumer-confidence indicator for the 21-nation currency area fell 1.0 point to minus 16.5 in September. A consensus of economists polled last week by The Wall Street Journal expected it to decline less steeply to minus 16.0.
Confidence had edged higher over the past few months, reaching in August its highest point since February, before the outbreak of the war in Iran that sharply darkened the mood among consumers.
